liam (runtime): Heads up — us-west GPU pool hit sustained 95% util for ~20m and tail latency for >8k token requests spiked. We got customer-facing traces showing 600–900ms extra per token.

maya (eng-infra): Oof. Is this the same burst pattern we saw last month or something different?

liam (runtime): Similar shape but more polarized per-route: embedding-heavy routes saturating a few V100 pools while short-chat routes starve. Current FIFO queueing means long requests block batch formation for short ones.

sam (sre): Do we have the per-route queue depth & age histograms? Can we see which tenants/routes are responsible?

liam (runtime): Quick metrics: `route=embeddings` qlen=72, avg_age=4.2s, p95_lat_increase=1.1s; `route=chat-short` qlen=10, avg_age=0.5s, p95_lat_increase=0.2s. GPU pool `us-west-1a-gpu-1` running at 96% mem, 92% SM util.

evie (product): From customer impact POV short-chat SLOs are more critical for core app flows — chat owners will be annoyed. But embeddings are heavy revenue. We need a fair tradeoff.

maya (eng-infra): Proposal: try a seniority-weighted admission controller that mixes per-route minimum reservation + priority weight + age-based promotion. That should avoid starvation while keeping predictable capacity for high-value routes.

liam (runtime): Sketch of config we could canary to a shard (keeps batching intact):
```yaml
admission:
  mode: hybrid
  per_route:
    embeddings: {reserve_slots: 0.15, base_weight: 1.0}
    chat-short: {reserve_slots: 0.10, base_weight: 2.0}
    default: {reserve_slots: 0.05, base_weight: 1.0}
  priority:
    aging_window_sec: 8
    age_boost_per_sec: 0.15  # weight multiplier per second in queue
  global:
    max_inflight: 1200
    emergency_fallback: cpu-pool: true
```

maya (eng-infra): Key bits: reserve_slots are fraction of GPU-concurrency for hard reservations; base_weight controls token-bucket drain order; age boost prevents long requests from starving. Emergency_fallback spins up small CPU-backed runners for best-effort embedding requests to protect low-latency chat.

sam (sre): Two concerns: 1) how this affects batching efficiency (we might reduce average batch size for embeddings) and 2) cost spike if fallback CPU kicks in. Need guardrails.

liam (runtime): Agree. Add a batching heuristic: allow embeddings to be batched across multiple small slots if pool occupancy < 80%, otherwise limit to same-route batching. Also add a cooldown for CPU fallback to avoid churn.

evie (product): Can we tie reserve_slots to revenue or SLO tags so product teams can self-declare importance? Like route metadata `sla:gold|silver|bronze` and cost center tag.

maya (eng-infra): Yes — plan to plumb route-level metadata from API gateway. We'll expose simple UI sliders in Console for reserve% and base_weight per route for enterprise customers.

deploy-bot: canary deployment queued: admission-controller v2.3 -> us-west-1a-gpu-1 (10% traffic).

ops-bot: experiment started. Monitoring chart `admission.seniority.weighted` and `queue.age.p95` added to `eng-infra/seniority-canary` dashboard.

sam (sre): For rollout: start with 3h canary, check batch_size, p50/p95/p99 latency for chat and embeddings, monitor cost delta for CPU fallback. If cost > +8% or chat_p99 regresses > 10% cancel.

liam (runtime): I'll wire in metrics and a prom alert and add a quick `kubectl` rollback playbook. MFA owner: @maya.

maya (eng-infra): I'll also produce a small synthetic driver to replay mixed workloads so we can iterate offline (keeps cluster costs small).

evie (product): Thanks — once we validate, we can turn on route-level controls for a few enterprise accounts as an opt-in. Communicate SLO changes clearly. :megaphone:

liam (runtime): One more note: consider an alternate cheap option — enforce per-request max-token caps for embeddings at the gateway for bursts. That reduces tail resource usage without infra changes. We can A/B both.

maya (eng-infra): Good idea. We'll run two canaries: (A) seniority-weighted admission w/ CPU fallback, (B) gateway token-cap + conservative FIFO. Compare latency & cost.

sam (sre): OK let's meet tomorrow 09:30 to review first 3h canary metrics. I'll post a calendar invite.

liam (runtime): Thanks team. Short follow-ups in thread: I'll paste the synthetic workload driver and the prometheus queries after I finish them.

ops-bot: alert muted for `us-west` CPU-fallback during canary window as requested by maya.
